## Materials and Methods

Full details are given in Supplementary Materials and Methods.

**Pipeline and reference panel.** A Nextflow workflow screened each library for papillomavirus reads with Kraken2 against a combined human/HPV database (a library was called HPV-positive at ≥ 10 papillomavirus reads), typed positives against the complete PaVE reference set (`r stats$panel_n` sequences) by STAR alignment, and classified early versus late viral transcripts. Code and configuration are available as stated in the Data Availability Statement.

**Cohort.** Public human RNA-seq runs were discovered through NCBI Entrez and assembled into a case/control design spanning productive controls (warts, condyloma), epidermodysplasia verruciformis, cutaneous neoplasia (cSCC, actinic keratosis), an unselected-skin null, and cell-line, engineered and non-permissive-tissue comparators. Group assignment used curated SRA metadata, with a small override table correcting studies whose submitted metadata is absent or misleading. Of the `r comma(stats$n_submitted)` libraries that entered the screen, `r comma(stats$n_screened)` returned a result (@suppfig-cohort-flow). The remaining `r comma(stats$n_unscreened)` produced no screening output, either because quality filtering at a 36 bp minimum discarded every read of a short-read library or because the download failed. They are counted in no denominator, because a library that was never screened is not a negative observation.

**Calling infection and productivity.** A reference was assigned when coverage breadth was at least 0.10 and mean depth at least 2. Every library that returned a Kraken2 report, including negatives, was scored as RPM, the depth-normalized burden used throughout: `r comma(stats$n_burden)` libraries, the sweep pooled with the targeted lesion cohorts and minus two excluded sets (amplicon and lesion-adjacent mucosa), of which `r comma(stats$n_both)` are also among the `r comma(stats$n_screened)` screened. Productive infection (the L1 criterion) required at least three L1 major-capsid reads, and a control-calibrated detection floor was set at the 5th-percentile RPM of non-cell-line productive controls (`r p1(stats$floor_rpm)` RPM).

**Independent DNA reservoir.** The presence data against which the transcriptional result is read come from a published petabase-scale papillomavirus catalog of the Logan assembly (Shen et al, 2026, eLife Reviewed Preprint), not from our own pipeline. Its released cluster-by-library table was re-tabulated by body site, with environmental and non-human skin runs excluded, and each contig cluster mapped to an HPV type and then to a genus through the same type-to-genus map used for our RNA catalogs. All quantities from it are compositions conditional on positivity rather than prevalences.

**Approvals and consent.** <!-- JID requires approvals and consent to be stated in the Methods, not only in the Ethics Statement (Information for Authors, read 2026-11-02), so this paragraph cannot be deleted outright. It is kept to the bare requirement: the approvals-and-consent fact, and the retrieval and preprocessing sentence that JID's reanalysis rule asks for. The legal basis belongs to the Ethics Statement and the source list to the Data Availability Statement; both were restated here until 2026-11-02, when TP pointed out the overlap. --> We collected no new human material and analyzed only anonymous, publicly archived data, so the work required no ethics committee review or participant consent; the Ethics Statement gives the basis. We retrieved libraries from the Sequence Read Archive by accession with `fasterq-dump`, and applied no preprocessing before the quality filtering and screening described above.

**Confounder control and statistics.** Sequencing depth entered every model as log~10~ library size. Library-selection chemistry was recovered from SRA `LibrarySelection` and, where that field is generic, from library-construction protocol text, resolving `r pp(stats$chem_pct)`% of libraries. Integration was inferred from the E1:E2 transcript ratio and validated against virus-host junctions and an independent graded cervical series. Logistic regressions were fitted and Fisher exact tests run in R, with Wilson intervals for proportions and a Bayesian reanalysis under weakly informative priors as a robustness check (@supptbl-bayes, @suppfig-bayes).
